summary: Initial discovery for Sandstone Analytics evaluating Redwood Private. Focus on VPC peering vs private endpoints, cross-region constraints (EU/NA data residency), egress controls, KMS integration, and regional model availability. Agreed next steps: share network checklist, region/account details, schedule pilot planning.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
VPC peering and transit gateway approach
Cross-region data residency and latency impact
Egress controls, firewall/NAT, and IP allowlisting
KMS / HSM integration and key management
Rollout strategy: canary, fallback to hosted
transcript: 00:00 Alex Moreno: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call?
00:07 Marta Ruiz: Marta here, CTO at Sandstone. We have Samir, Emily, Ravi on the line too.

00:15 Alex Moreno: Great. So objective today is to understand your networking and region constraints for Private deployment, and we can go deep on peering vs private endpoints. Priya will cover the technical bits.

00:30 Priya Shah: Hi team. Quick FYI, I'll ask about your CIDR space, transit gateway strategy, and whether you need egress through corporate firewall. Also need to know required AWS regions -- we have slightly different model variants available in some zones.

00:48 Samir Patel: We're primarily US-EAST-1 and EU-WEST-1. A couple of teams also use AP-SOUTHEAST-1 for latency reasons, but that's lower priority. Data residency: EU customer data must remain in EU for those datasets.

01:05 Priya Shah: Noted. For EU residency we typically recommend pinning model endpoints to the region, or deploying a private control plane in your VPC in that region. We can also route by policy so EU requests never leave eu-west-1.
01:22 Emily Cho: Quick question — how do you handle key management? We require KMS and an HSM-backed key for encryption in transit and at rest.

01:30 Jon Park: We support customer-managed KMS keys; for Private we can integrate with your KMS via IAM roles and, if needed, HSM-backed keys through AWS CloudHSM. We'll share the integration pattern and required IAM policies.

01:48 Marta Ruiz: Good. Another blocker is our networking team prefers not to allow full VPC peering due to route table complexity; they like private endpoints or interface endpoints instead. Curious on Redwood's recommended pattern.

02:02 Priya Shah: Both are supported. Peering/transit-gateway provides low-latency, full-mesh connectivity, useful when you want to avoid public egress. Interface endpoints (PrivateLink) are simpler and work well with restricted networking but have per-AZ ENI and costs per endpoint. There are trade-offs with cross-account routing too.
02:25 Samir Patel: Could you quantify cost or perf delta? We have tight latency SLOs for chat features — 95th percentile under 200ms.

02:35 Priya Shah: Peering gives slightly better p95 latency because traffic stays on the internal network, but if you put inference in the same AZ as your app, private endpoints are fine. For very high throughput, peering/transit gateway helps with flow limits.
02:50 Emily Cho: There's also audit/logging. If traffic routes through transit gateway we need flow logs tied to our SIEM.

02:57 Jon Park: We can emit connection-level logs and request traces to your logging endpoint; we also integrate with CloudWatch/VPC Flow Logs and can ship to your S3 or SIEM via Kinesis. We'll share example retention settings.
03:12 Ravi Kapoor: Regarding model versions — can we pin across regions? For example, the quantized variant we test in us-east should be identical in eu-west.
03:20 Priya Shah: We support model pinning and versioned rollouts. Some optimized kernels are hardware dependent; we'll flag any model compile differences per region upfront.
03:35 Samir Patel: On the IP allowlisting side, if we use PrivateLink do we still need to allow outbound to Redwood IPs?

03:42 Priya Shah: With interface endpoints you keep traffic inside AWS, so you wouldn't need public egress to Redwood's hosted internet IPs. If you use peering to a Redwood VPC, you'll need routes but no public egress either.
03:57 Unknown Speaker - contractor: sorry, quick interjection — our network team uses a small CIDR /22 per service. Will that be enough for ENIs?

04:04 Priya Shah: Depends on scale. For PrivateLink endpoints you need one ENI per AZ per endpoint and additional IPs for the control plane. We'll provide a CIDR guidance doc. For large scale you may prefer peering+transit gateway.
04:25 Alex Moreno: Let's pivot to security/compliance. Emily, what certifications do you need?
04:30 Emily Cho: SOC 2 Type II is mandatory, plus we want detailed audit logs, SSO via SAML, and role-based access control. Also need evidence of secure default configs and change management.
04:42 Jon Park: We have SOC2 docs; Priya will share the security pack. For SSO we support SAML/OIDC and can sync groups for RBAC at the route/model level.

04:55 Samir Patel: One more region-related item: latency between eu-west-1 and us-east for model-heavy features — if we keep EU-only data in eu-west, but product team wants inference in us-east for cost reasons, how do you handle data locality restrictions?

05:09 Priya Shah: You can set routing policy per route such that EU requests are routed to eu models. If you must call us-east for certain models, we recommend preprocessing in EU and sending only non-personalized tokens across regions — but that still can be a compliance issue.
05:25 Marta Ruiz: So likely we'll need eu-west deployment for EU customers. Ok.
05:30 Alex Moreno: On the pilot — what's a realistic minimal pilot? Priya?

05:34 Priya Shah: A pilot can be a single-region private deployment in your EU account: one model endpoint, canary traffic (10%), and synthetic load tests to validate p95 and cost. We'll define acceptance criteria — latency, error rate, and cost per token baseline.
05:52 Samir Patel: We need to know the firewall ports and exact ENI egress requirements. Also whether NAT gateway is required for control plane calls.

06:02 Priya Shah: We'll provide a list: VPC CIDR, subnets per AZ, security group rules (TCP 443 outbound to Redwood control plane endpoints if using hosted control plane), or if private control plane in-VPC then no outbound. We'll include sample security group and route table entries.
06:20 Emily Cho: Are audit logs tamper-evident? We will insist on S3 with Object Lock for retention during audits.
06:28 Jon Park: We can stream logs to your S3 bucket and support S3 Object Lock policy if required. We'll include recommended retention and hashing checks.
06:44 Ravi Kapoor: Any hard blockers around private DNS or split-horizon? Some of our microservices assume public hostnames.
06:52 Priya Shah: We support private DNS entries for endpoints. If you have split-horizon, we'll coordinate required hostnames and certificates. TLS termination is mutual TLS optionally.
07:05 Samir Patel: For mutual TLS, do you require client certs?
07:09 Jon Park: Mutual TLS is optional; we typically authenticate via IAM roles or mTLS for extra layer. We'll list supported auth patterns.
07:20 Marta Ruiz: About model updates — how disruptive are rollouts? We need a canary and automatic fallback to hosted models if private infra has issues.

07:29 Priya Shah: Rollouts support canary, A/B, and auto-fallback policies. If a private pool degrades beyond thresholds we can route to hosted or dedicated fallback. We'll document SLOs and expected failover times.
07:44 Unknown Speaker - contractor: transcription note — 'canary' sounded like 'canopy' earlier in the doc, ignore that.
07:52 Alex Moreno: Haha noted. Back to network egress — some customers force all egress through corporate egress appliances, is that supported?
08:00 Priya Shah: Yes — you can route control plane egress through your NAT or egress proxy; some customers do TLS inspection so keep in mind mutual TLS might be affected.
08:12 Emily Cho: We also need a list of Redwood's public IP ranges if we use allowlisting for on-prem firewalls.
08:18 Alex Moreno: We'll share the allowlist and it's also included in the private checklist spreadsheet.
08:27 Samir Patel: Any special constraints for APAC regions? We have one team considering Singapore. Are model variants fully available there?

08:35 Priya Shah: Some model variants are still rolling out in APAC; performance profiles differ by instance type and region. For APAC we recommend dedicated capacity or hosted shaped for that region. We'll include a region-availability table.
08:52 Ravi Kapoor: For cost considerations, what's the rough delta between hosted and private? We are cost-sensitive.

08:59 Jon Park: Private has a baseline infra cost (reserved pools or customer-managed infra) but reduces per-token egress and can reduce latency. We can run sizing based on your token estimates and provide a cost model.
09:10 Marta Ruiz: Let's talk about timeline — we want this in production for a pilot in Q3. Is that feasible?
09:16 Alex Moreno: Yes, typical pilot 4-6 weeks from kickoff depending on network approvals; cloud ops sign-off often the pacing item.
09:26 Emily Cho: For SSO, we want SCIM user sync. Do you support automatic provisioning?
09:32 Jon Park: Yes SCIM provisioning supported; we'll send SAML/SCIM integration docs.
09:42 Samir Patel: Are there any restrictions on Kubernetes env or EKS? We're thinking of running the app in EKS with sidecars to call Redwood private endpoints.
09:51 Priya Shah: That's a common pattern. You can run a sidecar or use an internal load balancer. We'll include an example K8s service and IAM role mapping for EKS.
10:05 Alex Moreno: I'm going to open the next steps — we'll send the checklist and diagrams. Anything else urgent?
10:12 Marta Ruiz: One more — can you do a short throughput benchmark with our typical prompt mix? We'll want to see p95 token latency with our prompts.
10:20 Priya Shah: Absolutely. For the pilot we'll run a smoke test with your prompt set. Please upload a small anonymized prompt corpus; we can do synthetic load as well.
10:30 Ravi Kapoor: We'll prepare that and anonymize PII.
10:34 Alex Moreno: Great. I'll recap the action items and share calendar invites for pilot planning. Thanks everyone.
10:40 Marta Ruiz: Thanks all. Looking forward to the checklist.
